newsitem.title: ITALY: Transport strike wreaks havoc in southern Italy.
newsitem.headline: Transport strike wreaks havoc in southern Italy.

text.p: A strike by bus, tram and commuter train workers wreaked havoc with traffic in southern Italy on Friday following stoppages that brought chaos to the centre and the north earlier this week.
Union leaders said they called the strikes to demand a renewal of workers' contracts which expired around nine months ago and to demand a reform of the local transport system.
Friday's stoppage hit most of southern Italy and Sicily but was called off in the Calabrian town of Crotone where recent heavy rains have brought normal activity to a standstill.
Transport workers in Rome have postponed participating in the strike until next Tuesday following an appeal by mayor Francesco Rutelli.
He feared that transport chaos would paint a poor picture of the city for visiting International Olympic Committee officials looking at Rome's bid to host the 2004 Summer Games.
The stoppages are due to be followed by a national strike called for October 25.
